Integumentary Drugs

Skin drugs — topical corticosteroids, antifungals, antiseptics, emollients and keratolytics.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List skin drug classes and examples
  • Describe uses of topical corticosteroids, antifungals and antiseptics
  • Explain nurse responsibilities in topical drug administration

In simple words

Skin drugs (dermatological drugs) are applied to the skin to treat skin conditions — eczema, fungal infections, acne, psoriasis and itching. They come as creams, ointments, lotions, powders and solutions.

Nurses apply topical drugs correctly and teach patients self-application.

Common skin drugs

Class Examples Use
Topical corticosteroids Hydrocortisone, betamethasone, clobetasol Reduce inflammation — eczema, dermatitis
Antifungals Clotrimazole, miconazole, terbinafine Treat fungal infections — ringworm, candidiasis
Antiseptics Chlorhexidine, povidone-iodine Clean wounds, prevent infection
Emollients Liquid paraffin, moisturisers Soften skin — eczema, dry skin
Keratolytics Salicylic acid Remove scales — warts, psoriasis
Topical antibiotics Mupirocin, fusidic acid Treat skin infections

Safe application

  • Wash hands before and after application.
  • Apply a thin layer — more is not better.
  • Avoid eyes, mouth and broken skin (unless ordered).
  • Wear gloves when applying to infected areas.
  • Do not use potent topical steroids on the face or for long periods without review.
  • Occlusive dressings increase absorption — use only as ordered.

🔴 Thin layer only

Apply topical drugs in a thin layer — more is not better. Avoid eyes, mouth and broken skin unless ordered; wear gloves for infected areas.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Apply topical drugs — wash hands, clean the area, apply thin layer, wash hands after.
  • Wear gloves — when applying to infected or exuding wounds.
  • Patient teaching — show how to apply; emphasize not sharing topical drugs; avoid eyes.
  • Monitor — watch for skin irritation, rash, worsening; report to doctor.
  • Steroid caution — potent topical steroids should not be used on the face or for long periods without medical review (skin thinning risk).

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Skin drugs are applied to the skin — creams, ointments, lotions, powders, solutions.
  2. Topical corticosteroids (e.g., hydrocortisone) reduce inflammation — eczema, dermatitis.
  3. Antifungals (e.g., clotrimazole) treat fungal infections — ringworm, candidiasis.
  4. Emollients soften dry skin; keratolytics (e.g., salicylic acid) remove scales.
  5. Apply a thin layer; wash hands before and after; avoid eyes.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Wear gloves when applying to infected or exuding areas.
  2. Potent topical steroids — not on the face or for long periods without review (skin thinning).
  3. Do not share topical drugs between patients.
  4. Occlusive dressings increase drug absorption — use only as ordered.

📌 Memory trick

Skin drug application: “Clean, Thin, Gloves, Wash” — clean area, thin layer, gloves for infected, wash hands.

60-second revision

  • Skin drugs = creams, ointments, lotions, powders, solutions.
  • Topical steroids reduce inflammation (eczema, dermatitis).
  • Antifungals treat fungal infections (ringworm, candidiasis).
  • Emollients soften dry skin; keratolytics remove scales.
  • Thin layer; wash hands; avoid eyes; gloves for infected areas.
  • Potent steroids — not on face/long term without review.

Test yourself

Topical corticosteroids are used for:

Answer: B. Topical corticosteroids reduce inflammation in conditions like eczema and dermatitis.

Which is an antifungal?

Answer: B. Clotrimazole is an antifungal used for ringworm and candidiasis.

Emollients are used for:

Answer: B. Emollients soften and moisturise dry skin — used in eczema and dry skin conditions.

Topical drugs should be applied:

Answer: B. Apply a thin layer — more is not better and can increase side effects.

Potent topical steroids should not be used on:

Answer: B. Potent topical steroids should not be used on the face (skin thinning risk) without medical review.
